# Reviewing changes to the agent skill set

These paths hold the repository's agent-facing instructions. The layout and the rules below exist to
stop the set drifting back into several copies of the same rule disagreeing with each other, which is
what `.agents/README.md` and `.agents/CHANGELOG.md` document. Flag any change that breaks them.

## Layout

Canonical skills live in exactly two places, each for a stated reason:

- `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — the default for a new skill. Codex scans this path.
- `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — only for skills gh-aw must see. The gh-aw compiler bakes
  `GH_AW_SKILL_DIR: ".github/skills"` into every `*.lock.yml`, so these cannot move.

Flag as a problem:

- A `SKILL.md` added anywhere else, including a new `.codex/`, `.ai/`, or root `skills/` directory.
  There is deliberately no `.codex/` directory: Codex reads `.agents/skills/` natively.
- A new skill that is not added to the **The skills** table in `.agents/README.md`.
- A `SKILL.md` without YAML frontmatter carrying both `name` and `description`. Without them the
  skill cannot be discovered by any tool.

## Generated pointer files

`.claude/skills/**` is generated by `scripts/sync-agent-skills.mjs`. Claude Code discovers project
skills only from `.claude/skills/`, so every canonical skill needs a pointer there.

Flag as a problem:

- Any hand-edit to a file under `.claude/skills/`. Each one says "Generated … Do not edit".
- Rules, procedures or examples added to a pointer. A pointer carries only the canonical `name` and
  `description` plus a redirect.
- A changed `name` or `description` in a canonical `SKILL.md` with no matching change under
  `.claude/skills/` in the same commit. The author needs to run `npm run skills:sync`. The
  `description` is the triggering surface and must match the canonical byte for byte.
- A skill directory removed from `.agents/skills/` or `.github/skills/` while its pointer remains.

## One rule, one place

The set's anti-drift rule: a rule is stated once, in the canonical file, and referenced everywhere
else.

Flag as a problem:

- Frontmatter or `llms.description` rules restated in `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`, a README, or a
  skill other than `igniteui-topic-frontmatter`. CONTRIBUTING may state limits the build enforces
  (`npm run check:llms-metadata`) and must link to
  `.agents/skills/igniteui-topic-frontmatter/references/audit-rules.md` for everything else.
- Topic structure, heading or template rules stated outside
  `.agents/skills/igniteui-doc-topics/references/house-style.md`.
- `ApiLink` markup rules stated outside `.github/skills/xplat-docs-api-links/SKILL.md`.
  `docs/xplat/API-LINKS-README.md` and `docs/xplat/API-REFERENCES.md` are human background only and
  must not be turned back into agent instructions.
- A new agent-facing guide added under `docs/xplat/` (for example an `AI-AGENT-*.md` file). Two such
  guides were removed because they contradicted the skills; new guidance belongs in a skill.

## ApiLink markup

The registry resolves package, prefix, suffix and member anchors. No file under
`docs/xplat/src/content/en/` uses `prefixed` or `suffix`.

Flag as a problem:

- Guidance or examples that reintroduce `prefixed={false}` or `suffix={false}`, or that tell an
  author to restore them after a docfx sync.
- Guidance that `pkg=` is required. It is for disambiguation only, when `check-mdx-links` reports
  the same symbol in more than one package.
- Guidance to add `exclude`, `excludePrefixFor` or `excludeSuffixFor`. Those props are obsolete.

## Version discipline

Files in the doc-skill set (`.agents/skills/igniteui-doc-topics/**`,
`.agents/skills/igniteui-topic-frontmatter/**`, `.agents/README.md`, `.agents/CHANGELOG.md`) carry a
`Version: vN · date · igniteui doc-skill set` line, and they all move together.

Flag as a problem:

- A rule change in one of those files without the version line bumped across the set.
- A rule change with no corresponding entry in `.agents/CHANGELOG.md` recording what changed, why,
  and the finding or decision ID it traces to.
- A `‹VERIFY: …›` placeholder deleted rather than resolved. Each is listed in the changelog with an
  owner, and resolving one means applying its pre-committed outcome in the same edit.
